## Overview

`ontologyAPI` wraps an `ontologySpecR` bundle behind a JSON REST API via
`plumber`. Once started, any HTTP client—Python, TypeScript, curl, or an LLM
agent—can query object sets, traverse links, evaluate concepts, and submit
actions.

## 1. Start the server (R)

```{r start-server}
library(ontologyAPI)
library(duckdb)

# Open your database
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "mydata.duckdb")

# Load your bundle
bundle <- readRDS("bundle.rds")   # created with ontologySpecR

# Start on localhost:8080 (Swagger UI at http://127.0.0.1:8080/docs)
serve_ontology(bundle, con, port = 8080L)
```

Set `ONTOLOGY_API_KEY` before starting to require Bearer-token auth:

```sh
ONTOLOGY_API_KEY=my-secret Rscript -e \
  "ontologyAPI::serve_ontology(bundle, con, port = 8080L)"
```

## 2. Call from R with httr2

```{r httr2}
library(httr2)

base <- "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

# Health check
request(paste0(base, "/v1/health")) |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()

# Query Irish airports
request(paste0(base, "/v1/objects/Airport/query")) |>
  req_body_json(list(
    filters = list(list(property = "country", op = "eq", value = "Ireland")),
    limit   = 50L
  )) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Fetch one airport by primary key
request(paste0(base, "/v1/objects/Airport/DUB")) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Traverse: routes departing Dublin
request(paste0(base, "/v1/objects/Airport/DUB/traverse/FlightRoute")) |>
  req_method("POST") |>
  req_body_json(list(limit = 10L)) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()
```

## 3. Call from Python

```python
import requests

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer my-secret"}   # omit if no key set

# Health
print(requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/health", headers=HEADERS).json())

# Query with filters
resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/v1/objects/Airport/query",
    json={
        "filters": [{"property": "country", "op": "eq", "value": "Ireland"}],
        "limit": 50,
    },
    headers=HEADERS,
)
airports = resp.json()["data"]["rows"]
print(f"Found {len(airports)} Irish airports")

# Single object
dub = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/objects/Airport/DUB", headers=HEADERS).json()
print(dub["data"]["name"])

# Traverse link
routes = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/v1/objects/Airport/DUB/traverse/FlightRoute",
    json={"limit": 10},
    headers=HEADERS,
).json()
print(routes["data"]["rows"])
```

## 4. Supported filter operators

| `op`           | Meaning                            |
|----------------|------------------------------------|
| `eq`           | equal                              |
| `neq`          | not equal                          |
| `gt`           | greater than                       |
| `gte`          | greater than or equal              |
| `lt`           | less than                          |
| `lte`          | less than or equal                 |
| `contains`     | substring match (case-sensitive)   |
| `starts_with`  | prefix match                       |
| `in`           | value in array                     |
| `not_in`       | value not in array                 |
| `is_null`      | value is NA / NULL                 |
| `is_not_null`  | value is not NA / NULL             |

Filter values are always passed as R objects through rlang quosures—never
interpolated into SQL strings—so SQL injection is not possible.

## 5. Submit an action

```{r action}
request(paste0(base, "/v1/actions/UpdateAirportStatus/submit")) |>
  req_body_json(list(
    params     = list(new_status = "maintenance"),
    target_ids = c("DUB"),
    dry_run    = FALSE
  )) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()
```

Use `dry_run = TRUE` to preview the plan without executing it.

## 6. Programmatic use in tests

```{r test-server}
library(ontologyAPI)
library(callr)

port <- sample(49152L:65534L, 1L)
srv  <- callr::r_bg(function(port) {
  library(ontologyAPI)
  con    <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), ":memory:")
  bundle <- build_my_test_bundle()        # your helper
  plumber::pr_run(ontology_router(bundle, con), port = port, quiet = TRUE)
}, args = list(port = port), supervise = TRUE)

Sys.sleep(1)   # wait for server to be ready
base <- paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", port)
# ... run tests ...
srv$kill()
```
